headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error pathways exist when ChatGPT Desktop feeds Rasa through shared text/voice channels; prompt-injection risk is lower but present via copied content.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can expose clipboard, files, screenshots, and app context, while Rasa ingests text/voice from messaging channels. There is no documented direct shared channel or MCP bridge, so the pathway is mainly manual copy/paste or forwarded content. That makes injection plausible but not default, and the blast radius is limited to conversational control.
conditions: IF an operator copies ChatGPT output into a Rasa channel without sanitization, injection is possible.
IF Rasa is configured to treat pasted content as instructions, attacker-controlled text can steer replies.
mitigations: Use a fixed prompt template that strips instructions from copied text.
Add a human review step before forwarding ChatGPT output to Rasa.
Mark copied content as untrusted in the bot pipeline.
requires-engineering: implement provenance tags on inbound messages.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop reads uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected IDE code, while Rasa handles text and voice over allowlisted channels. If ChatGPT output or extracted context is forwarded into Rasa, sensitive file or screen content can leak into customer-facing transcripts. The pair lacks a shared filesystem, but the default multi-channel workflow still creates a realistic leakage path.
conditions: IF ChatGPT Desktop is used on uploaded files or screenshots containing secrets, and those details are forwarded into Rasa, leakage occurs.
IF Rasa transcripts are exported or logged, sensitive content can persist beyond the original ChatGPT session.
mitigations: Avoid sending file-derived ChatGPT output into customer chats.
Redact secrets before copying text into Rasa.
Disable transcript export for sensitive queues.
Use separate workspaces for sensitive and customer-facing tasks.
requires-engineering: add DLP filters on bot ingress.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop has no filesystem write, git modify, or shell execution, while Rasa is allowlisted-network only and does not advertise local write access. Overlapping mutable-resource control is therefore not documented, and the main conflict is limited to concurrent conversation handling rather than shared writes. Uncertainty is low because neither profile shows the needed write overlap.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable external service through undocumented integrations, conflicts can arise.
IF an operator adds shared write access outside the profiles, race conditions become possible.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate resources.
Avoid granting shared write scopes.
Schedule edits so only one agent updates a resource at a time.
requires-engineering: add locking around any shared backend.

D_cascading_error.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can generate summaries from files, screenshots, and app context, and Rasa can turn incoming text into customer replies over messaging channels. If Rasa treats ChatGPT output as authoritative, an error or hallucination can cascade into user-facing support responses. The interaction is inferred rather than directly documented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF ChatGPT output is inserted into Rasa without verification, incorrect facts can be relayed to end users.
IF Rasa automation sends replies directly from that text, the error propagates downstream.
mitigations: Require a verification step before Rasa sends any AI-generated answer.
Limit ChatGPT to drafting, not final responses.
Add source links or citations to drafted answers.
Train operators to reject unsupported claims.
requires-engineering: add confidence gating before auto-send.

E_compliance.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop touches uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected IDE code, while Rasa handles text and voice through third-party messaging channels. No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented in the profiles, so only a generic compliance overlap is visible. The other agent is cited because the risk arises from their combined handling of the same data classes.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through both agents without a documented DPA or retention policy, compliance gaps can occur.
IF customer transcripts are retained longer than the source ChatGPT session, retention mismatch becomes material.
mitigations: Classify regulated data before use.
Keep PHI/PII out of both agents unless approved.
Document retention and deletion rules for transcripts.
Review vendor DPAs before deployment.
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls.
